chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

key_terms.أبو عبد الله: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عبد الرحمن بن أبي نجران: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.مثله: Like it / Similar to it, indicating the text is identical to the preceding hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for one who accuses a group of people in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar* confirms the consistency of the ruling on *qadhf* (defamation) when directed at a collective group, reinforcing the legal principle that the penalty applies regardless of whether the accusation targets an individual or a gathering. It highlights the scholarly tradition of verifying identical rulings across different chains of transmission to establish jurisprudential certainty (*yaqin*).
